threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the Tube to be on time. We know it’s a fantasy. Locals roll their eyes and plan for delays like it’s part of the day.
Caught the N59 last night; a guy was serenading the whole bus with classic R&B, and surprisingly, everyone joined in. Best late-night vibe ever.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a street vendor selling homemade kebabs next to a protest for better public transport. That's Neukölln for you, always juggling flavors and voices.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find a random open-air cinema in a former car park, where locals set up picnic blankets and share homemade snacks. Pure Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals know to walk half a block around the Civic Center to avoid the BART chaos when there's a delay. Visitors just stand there, perplexed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni delayed today because a dog decided the tracks were its new favorite sunbathing spot. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas, but many locals just grab a sandwich from the bakery. The real snack scene hides in the back streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll catch them standing cluelessly at the metro ticket machines, pressing buttons like it's a game show. Locals know to just hop on.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of just 'the train' like everyone else. It's an instant giveaway, mate.
Caught a glimpse of a bloke serenading the night bus crew with a ukulele on the 35. Only in Brixton, I swear!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you realize the guy selling Berlinschnitzel on the corner knows your order by heart after just a few visits. That's when you really belong.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Neukölln can you find a bar that doubles as a thrift shop and a craft fair. One night you're sipping cocktails, the next you're browsing vintage clothes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their skill at dodging BART delays. If they know all the coffee spots near the Civic Center that stay open during emergencies, they’re homegrown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 6 bus stuck at a red light while a marching band passed by. Only in SF do the delays come with a soundtrack.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think La Rambla is the heart of Barcelona, but real life pulses in the small plazas of Gràcia, where the local kids play and families gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their bewilderment at the metro ticket machines; locals know it’s cash only after 9 PM.
